methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $575M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
VulcanForms is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Hart and Martin Feldmann that has raised $575M+ to date. The relevant peer universe comprises 10 companies in the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including 1 public company (277810.KQ) and 8 private peers such as Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables with similar valuation tiers to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the applicable triangulation method. Using total capital raised ($575M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage progression, the analysis yields an implied valuation of $690M. This represents the single quantitative anchor available from the provided dataset.

The triangulated range is $586M (low) to $793M (high), centered on the $690M median derived from stage-progression. The narrow methodological foundation—relying on a single applicable approach rather than cross-validation across multiple methods—represents the primary valuation uncertainty. Additionally, absence of late-stage comparable transactions in the narrow peer set limits confidence in the 1.2x multiplier assumption. Definitive valuation would require either identification of additional same-stage robotics comps or access to transaction multiples within the existing peer cohort.
